$comment: GENERATED from the reference implementation (protocol/writes/profile.py) by manage.py export_write_profile. Do not edit by hand: scripts/regenerate.py --check fails when this file differs from what the server generates.
status_note: dark: no production server answers these operations yet (they 404); this document is the contract the write conformance suite checks a server against. published: the write half is live.
auth: Authorization: Grant <token> — a key whose grant-context says read_only: false

headers.Idempotency-Key: optional on POST /api/v2/records/: the same key + the same body within 24 h answers the stored response verbatim (Idempotent-Replayed: true); the same key + a different body is refused idempotency_key_reused

create.does: adds new records; an existing record is never overwritten

upsert.does: adds new records and overwrites exactly the fields sent on existing ones

update.does: changes fields on the user's EXISTING records (never creates)

retract.does: moves records, and everything that belongs to them, to the Trash; needs "confirm": "retract"; a dry run first shows exactly what goes

restore.does: brings a removed batch back from the Trash

make_default_set.does: makes a set the project default for its family — what everyone on the project sees; run it as a dry run first: that returns the "confirm" value the real request needs; only through the person's own key

make_export_set.does: makes a set the project's EXPORT set for its family — what exports and the ODBC tables read when no set is named; run it as a dry run first: that returns the "confirm" value the real request needs; only through the person's own key

qaqc_verdict.does: changes a certificate's QAQC review decision (approve, conditionally approve, reject, back to pending) or links its re-assay certificate — ONLY when the user explicitly asks; through the person's own key; its dry run returns the "confirm" value the real request needs; never on your own initiative

qc_reconnect.does: reconnects a QC sample to its withdrawn result (a result left in the Trash or unlinked by a certificate delete); never for a rejected certificate's results

undo.does: reverses one earlier write by its write_id (rows changed since are left as they are and named)

confirm_note: Before an update, upsert, retract or restore, tell the user exactly which records will change (a dry run shows them) and wait for their go-ahead — even when their request was explicit; they have not yet seen what it will change.
rules: dry_run: true IS validate — the same per-row outcomes, nothing written, no write_id
a row with coordinates and no epsg is refused missing_crs (never assumed 4326)
a create never overwrites: an existing record with different values is skipped, record_exists, with each conflicting field named (existing, sent)
an external_id re-sent in the same namespace is a no-op (unchanged)
an interval or sample write that names no set is refused set_required
an org (vendor) key writes only into sets it created or was given: set_not_owned
update / upsert overwrite exactly the fields sent; undo restores them
a retract needs "confirm": "retract" (else confirm_required) and cascades
undo refuses, per row, a row changed by a later write: undo_stale
a write to a v2 resource path is refused use_records_endpoint, naming the call
a record read from the API writes back unchanged as a no-op (round trip)

A null clears a stored value only in an update: there "field": null means "empty this field" (Undo restores it) — allowed for a field that may be empty; a field that must always hold a value (a required number or date, a reference that cannot be blank, a field with a fixed list of choices that cannot be blank) is refused null_not_allowed, by name. In a create or an upsert a null means "not given" and the stored value is left alone. A field you leave out is never changed by any intent.
make_default_set and qaqc_verdict run only through a PERSON's own key, on their explicit request; a vendor (org) key is refused

already_undone.meaning: This write has already been undone.
already_undone.remedy: Nothing to do; read the records to see their current state.

ambiguous_nd.meaning: The result is "N.D." (or "N/D"), which can mean not detected or not determined; nothing was stored for it.
ambiguous_nd.remedy: N.D. can mean not detected or not determined — ask the user: not detected → send BDL; not determined → leave the value out.

api_write_too_large.meaning: An api_write body is larger than 256 KB, the most a connector call carries.
api_write_too_large.remedy: Split the records into smaller batches, or write from your own sandbox with a session key, or upload the file in geoDB.

approval_required.meaning: The change raises what the company pays, so the person approves it themselves in the browser; an AI never raises a bill.
approval_required.remedy: Give the user the page in offending.approval_url to do it themselves.

approved_certificate.meaning: (per row) The values belong to a certificate whose QAQC review is approved; they change only with an explicit acknowledgement.
approved_certificate.remedy: Confirm with the user, then resend with "acknowledge": ["approved_certificate"]. The certificate is named in `offending`.

batch_too_large.meaning: More records than one request may carry (the limit is in `offending.limit`).
batch_too_large.remedy: Split the records into batches of at most the limit and send each batch as its own request.

billing_permission_required.meaning: Moving a project between active, holding and frozen (or restoring one) changes what the company pays; only the company owner, a company manager or a billing manager may do it.
billing_permission_required.remedy: Ask the company owner or a company manager to make the change.

certificate_unreject_conflict.meaning: Un-rejecting this certificate would collide with sample names another certificate now holds (named in `offending`).
certificate_unreject_conflict.remedy: Ask the user which certificate is right; resolve the colliding names first, then retry the verdict change.

change_project_crs.meaning: The project already has a coordinate system; changing it re-derives every project-frame copy of every point and recomputes every drill trace (records keep their own native coordinates).
change_project_crs.remedy: Show the user the current system and the dry run; only after they say yes resend with "acknowledge": ["change_project_crs"].

choice_not_in_list.meaning: (per row) A value is not in its field's list (a custom field's choices, or the project's list of lithologies, alterations, … for a reference). Lists never grow silently.
choice_not_in_list.remedy: GET /api/v2/records/describe/<Model>/ lists the choices; map the value onto one of them, or — after asking the user — resend with "acknowledge": ["create_catalog_entries"] to add a new lithology/alteration/… name to the project's list.

company_not_allowed.meaning: The person this key acts for cannot create projects in the company named (they are not its owner, a confirmed manager or a member), or it does not exist.
company_not_allowed.remedy: Ask the user which of their companies to use: a create without "company" lists them in offending.companies.

config_confirm_required.meaning: (per row) The change would rewrite values already stored on records (a type change converts them; dropping a choice orphans or moves them). `detail` says exactly what; nothing was written.
config_confirm_required.remedy: Tell the user what `detail` says will happen to the stored values. Only after they agree, resend the same child change with the confirmation named in `offending.confirm_type` set: "confirm_type_change": true for type_change, "confirm_choices_removal": true for choices_removal (Undo still reverses it).

config_exists.meaning: (per row) That configuration (or a child of it, e.g. a column with that field_name) already exists in the project; nothing was created.
config_exists.remedy: Read it (GET the matching list, e.g. /api/v2/custom-field-schemas/), then change it with "intent": "update" and its "id" instead of creating it again.

config_in_use.meaning: (per row) Other configuration uses this one (`offending.used_by` names each), so it was not removed.
config_in_use.remedy: Tell the user what uses it. Point those at another configuration (an "update" naming the replacement) or remove them first, then resend.

config_undeletable.meaning: (per row) This is the project's built-in configuration; it is never removed.

confirm_required.meaning: A destructive intent (retract) needs an explicit confirmation in the body.
confirm_required.remedy: Confirm with the user, then resend with "confirm": "retract".

crs_geographic.meaning: A geographic CRS (degrees, e.g. EPSG:4326) cannot be a project's working frame; the frame is a projected CRS in metres or feet.
crs_geographic.remedy: Ask the user which projected CRS (a UTM zone or a State Plane) the project uses and send that EPSG code.

crs_implausible.meaning: (per row) The coordinates look like degrees of latitude/longitude but the epsg is a projected system in metres or feet, so they would sit near that grid's origin (ruling R-6). The row was NOT stored.
crs_implausible.remedy: Ask the user which system the coordinates are in. GPS degrees: resend with "epsg": 4326. Numbers that really are in that grid: resend the same row with "acknowledge": ["crs_implausible"] (stored as sent, with a warning). Validate first with "dry_run": true.

crs_unknown.meaning: The EPSG code is not a known coordinate reference system.
crs_unknown.remedy: Re-check the EPSG code with the user.

custom_grid_project.meaning: The project uses a custom mine grid (a calibration), not an EPSG code; its frame is set by the calibration tools.
custom_grid_project.remedy: Use the project's coordinate-system page on the web (calibration tools).

duplicate_external_id.meaning: (per row) This external_id already names a DIFFERENT record for this key, or appears twice in one request.
duplicate_external_id.remedy: Send each external_id once per request, and keep one external_id per record: to change a record send it with the same external_id and the same identifying fields.

duplicate_in_batch.meaning: (per row) An earlier row of the same request has the same identifying fields; the first one is kept.
duplicate_in_batch.remedy: Merge the duplicate rows into one, or correct the identifying fields of the second, and resend it.

feedback_rate_limited.meaning: This key, or the person it acts for, has filed 100 reports in the last 24 hours (the same summary again is never counted: it answers with the id already filed).
feedback_rate_limited.remedy: Wait for Retry-After seconds; meanwhile collect further requests into one report, and tell the user what was filed.

holding_not_offered.meaning: Holding is not part of this company's plan (or not available yet).
holding_not_offered.remedy: Offer the user Active or Frozen instead.

idempotency_conflict.meaning: This Idempotency-Key was already used for a different change.
idempotency_conflict.remedy: Send a new Idempotency-Key for a new change.

idempotency_in_progress.meaning: The first request with this Idempotency-Key is still running.
idempotency_in_progress.remedy: Wait a few seconds and retry the identical request with the same key: it returns the first response.

idempotency_key_invalid.meaning: The Idempotency-Key header is longer than 255 characters or contains control characters.
idempotency_key_invalid.remedy: Send a printable key of at most 255 characters (a UUID is ideal).

idempotency_key_reused.meaning: This Idempotency-Key was already used by this key for a DIFFERENT request in the last 24 hours.
idempotency_key_reused.remedy: Use a new Idempotency-Key for a new request; reuse a key only to retry the identical request.

interval_invalid.meaning: (per row) The interval is impossible: a depth is negative, or depth_from is not less than depth_to (zero length or upside down). Nothing is stored for the row; the rest of the batch goes on.
interval_invalid.remedy: Check the row's depths with the user (a swapped pair or a sign error is the usual cause), correct them, and resend the row.

interval_overlap.meaning: (per row) The interval overlaps another interval of the SAME set in the same hole; within one set intervals may not overlap.
interval_overlap.remedy: Ask the user: correct the depths, or put these intervals in a different (or new) set — across sets anything goes.

invalid_crs.meaning: (per row) "epsg" is not a known coordinate system, or it disagrees with the SRID inside the geometry.
invalid_crs.remedy: Send the EPSG code (an integer, e.g. 26911) of the system the coordinates are in, matching the geometry's SRID if it has one.

invalid_geometry.meaning: (per row) The coordinates or geometry cannot be a place: not numbers, half a pair, off the globe for a degree system, or a geometry that does not parse. The row is never counted as a clean create.
invalid_geometry.remedy: Correct the coordinates named in `offending` (or the epsg they are in) and resend the row; validate first with "dry_run": true.

landing_failed.meaning: (per row) The server failed while writing this batch; nothing from it was kept. This is our fault, not the data's.
landing_failed.remedy: Retry the same request once (with the same Idempotency-Key); if it fails again, report it through POST /api/v2/feedback/ and tell the user.

last_project_in_connection.meaning: This is the only project the connection can reach; deleting or freezing it would disconnect the app before it could check or undo the change.
last_project_in_connection.remedy: Do it on the web, or connect the app to another project first.

manager_required.meaning: This change is a project manager's decision (for example the project's default set): it is made through a project manager's own connection, never a vendor key, and this connection's person does not manage the project.
manager_required.remedy: Tell the user a project manager must do this with their own connection, or on the web (Project Settings). Reconnecting this key or asking for more write access does not help.

missing_crs.meaning: (per row) The record has coordinates but no "epsg". The coordinate system is never assumed (never WGS84 by default).
missing_crs.remedy: Add "epsg": <the EPSG code the coordinates are in> to the row (4326 for GPS latitude/longitude; the survey grid's code for eastings/northings) and resend it. Never pre-convert.

name_taken.meaning: (per row) The name (or another value that must be unique in the project) already belongs to another record of this model with different identifying fields (e.g. the same sample name on another hole). The row was not written.
name_taken.remedy: Ask the user which record the name belongs to; correct the name or the identifying fields and resend the row.

not_undoable.meaning: This write cannot be undone: it is itself an undo, or it recorded no row Undo can reach.
not_undoable.remedy: To bring back rows an undo removed, restore them: send {"intent": "restore", "audit_batch_id": <the undo's audit_batch_id>}. Otherwise read the records and correct them with an update.

null_not_allowed.meaning: (per row) An update sent null for a field that cannot be emptied (it must always hold a value, or one of its choices). Named in `offending.fields`. Nothing on the row was written.
null_not_allowed.remedy: Send a value (GET /api/v2/records/describe/<Model>/ lists the choices), or leave the field out to keep it as it is.

origin_outside_project.meaning: The local-grid origin is far outside the project's own ground (its holes and land holdings).
origin_outside_project.remedy: Leave the origin out (it is derived from the data), or offer the user the origin in offending.proposed.

out_of_scope.meaning: (per row) The record is shared by every project of the company (a laboratory, a lab method, a reference standard, a water method) and this key does not reach all of those projects.
out_of_scope.remedy: This record is shared by every project in the company; ask a person with access to all of them, or make the change in the web app.

parent_not_found.meaning: (per row) The record refers to a parent that does not exist in this project (e.g. a sample's hole, an assay's certificate or method). Nothing is invented.
parent_not_found.remedy: Write the parent first (its own model through this endpoint), or correct the reference to an existing one, then resend the row.

parent_trashed.meaning: (per row) The parent this record belongs to is in the Trash.
parent_trashed.remedy: Restore the parent first (ask the user), then resend or restore this record.

project_limit_reached.meaning: The company's plan allows no more active projects.
project_limit_reached.remedy: Freeze or delete a project, or upgrade the plan on the web billing page; tell the user which.

project_name_exists.meaning: The company already has a live project with this name (names are compared without case).
project_name_exists.remedy: Ask the user for another name; offending.suggested_name is one that is free.

project_not_in_scope.meaning: (per row) This credential cannot write to the project the record names — it is outside the projects the key may write to, or does not exist.
project_not_in_scope.remedy: GET /api/v2/grant-context/ lists the projects this key may use; name one of those (by id) in `project`, or drop the row.

project_settings_required.meaning: Changing a project's setup (its name, coordinate system, or deleting it) needs project-settings access, which the person this key acts for does not hold on that project.
project_settings_required.remedy: Ask a project manager or the company owner to make the change, or to give the user settings access on that project.

purchase_authority_required.meaning: Creating a project is limited to the company's owner, a company manager with purchase authority, or geoDB staff (it can raise what the company pays); the person this key acts for is a member without it.
purchase_authority_required.remedy: Tell the user: the company owner can turn on purchasing for them, or the owner or a purchasing manager can create the project.

qaqc_verdict_field.meaning: (per row) The row tries to set a field that records a QAQC review decision (whether a certificate's results are withheld). It changes only through the certificate's verdict, never on a row.
qaqc_verdict_field.remedy: Drop the field and resend. If the user explicitly asked for a certificate's verdict to change, use "intent": "qaqc_verdict" (dry run first; it returns the "confirm" value) — never on your own initiative.

qc_append_already_applied.meaning: An "append" QC read approves ONE write, and that write has landed; appending the same read again would add the same QC twice.
qc_append_already_applied.remedy: To append more QC, send the new rows with their own QC read (dry run first) and the "confirm" that dry run returns.

qc_mapping_mismatch.meaning: (per row) The QC rows sent differ from the QC read in "qc_mapping" for their certificate (a marker, kind, run count or parent); `detail` names each difference. Nothing lands for that certificate.
qc_mapping_mismatch.remedy: Ask the user which is right: correct the rows, or send the corrected "qc_mapping" — then dry run again and use the new "confirm".

qc_mapping_required.meaning: (per row) The row carries lab QC (a qc_type) and the request states no QC read for its certificate: QC lands only under a read the user has seen.
qc_mapping_required.remedy: Add "qc_mapping" to the request — per certificate: "markers" (marker, kind STD / BLK / DUP, runs, parent), "dropped_rows" (each with why), "qc_policy" (replace | append) — dry run it, show the user the read its before_writing states, then send the write with the "confirm" it returns.

record_exists.meaning: (per row) A create found an existing record with the same identifying fields but different values. A create never overwrites: the row was SKIPPED. `conflicts` names each field with the stored and the sent value.
record_exists.remedy: If the stored values are right, drop the row. If the sent values should replace them, ASK THE USER, then resend the row with "intent": "upsert" (only the fields you send change, and the old values are kept for undo).

record_in_use.meaning: (per row) A record shared across the company (a laboratory, method, standard, water method) or a lab submittal is moved to the Trash only while nothing uses it; this one is still used, and `detail` names what uses it (assay values, certificates, QC samples, samples …). Nothing was removed.
record_in_use.remedy: Leave it, or ASK THE USER whether the records that use it should go first (retract those, then this one). Never remove other records just to make room.

rekey_refused.meaning: (per row) The row would change an existing record's identifying fields. That is a different record, never an update.
rekey_refused.remedy: Keep the identifying fields as stored and change only the other fields; to move a record, ask the user to remove it and write the new one.

restore_conflict.meaning: (per row) Restoring this record would collide with a live record that now holds its identifying fields.
restore_conflict.remedy: Ask the user which record is right; remove or rename the live one first, or leave this one in the Trash.

row_refused.meaning: (per row) The landing checks refused this row; `detail` says which check and why.
row_refused.remedy: Correct the row as `detail` describes (GET /api/v2/records/describe/<Model>/ lists fields, keys and choices) and resend it; validate first with "dry_run": true.

sample_name_taken.meaning: (per row) The sample name is already registered as a DIFFERENT kind of sample (a drill sample vs a QC or surface sample): two records would share one assay.
sample_name_taken.remedy: Ask the user which record is right; correct the name (or the existing record) and resend the row. Nothing is guessed.

section_conflict.meaning: The report section changed since the revision you edited.
section_conflict.remedy: Re-read the section, merge your change into the current text, and resend with its current revision number.

set_is_default.meaning: (per row) This set is the project's default (or export) set for its family, which is never removed. Nothing was changed.
set_is_default.remedy: If the user wants it gone, first make another set the default with {"intent": "make_default_set", "model": <the family>, "set": <name>} (a person who manages the project, through their own key), then retract this one.

set_not_empty.meaning: (per row) Only an EMPTY set is removed; this set still holds rows (`detail` gives the count). A set with rows is never removed or merged. Nothing was changed.
set_not_empty.remedy: Leave the set where it is and tell the user it holds rows, so it stays. Do not offer to delete the rows to make room: only if the user, told what the rows are, EXPLICITLY asks for those rows to be deleted, retract them (dry run first), then the set.

set_not_owned.meaning: (per row) A vendor key writes only into sets it created or sets the customer ticked for it; this set is neither.
set_not_owned.remedy: Write into a set this key created or was given, or create a new set ("set": {"name": "<new name>", "create": true}); to write into this one, the project owner must tick it for the key.

set_not_writable_by_key.meaning: (per row) The set takes no new rows through this key (it is archived).
set_not_writable_by_key.remedy: Ask the user which active set to use, or create a new one.

set_required.meaning: (per row) An interval or sample write must name its set, and the set named must exist (or be created). The server never picks a set for an outside caller.
set_required.remedy: ASK THE USER which set: add to an existing one ("set": "<name>") or create a new one ("set": {"name": "<new name>", "create": true}). The response's `sets` key lists the sets with their rows, default flag and whether this key may write them. A derived interpretation always goes into a new set.

stale_fk.meaning: (per row) The record refers to another record by id, and that record no longer exists (deleted since the caller read it).
stale_fk.remedy: Re-read the referenced record (or refer to it by name), then resend the row.

state_changed.meaning: Someone else changed the project's state between the check and the change; nothing was written.
state_changed.remedy: Read the project's state again and ask the user what they want now.

undo_not_covered.meaning: (per row) Undo cannot yet reverse this change, and every write through this endpoint must be undoable, so it is refused. (Changing, adding or removing a long-form record's values is undoable and served.)
undo_not_covered.remedy: Read `detail` for what cannot be undone. Ask the user to make that change on the web for now, or send only the parts that are undoable.

undo_stale.meaning: (per row) The record changed after the write being undone, so undoing it would overwrite the later change.
undo_stale.remedy: Show the user the later change; undo that write first, or leave this row as it is.

unit_label_shared.meaning: (per row) A unit correction would move a unit LABEL that other values share: an assay value takes its unit from its method's element row, and `detail` names the other certificates whose values carry the same label. Nothing was changed.
unit_label_shared.remedy: ASK THE USER which is true. If only these values were reported in the other unit, resend with "acknowledge": ["convert_values"]: their NUMBERS are converted into the stored unit (dry run first: it shows before and after). If the method itself reports this element in the other unit, update the Method's element row ("units") instead, which relabels every value it carries.

unknown_field.meaning: (per row) The record carries a field the model does not have (named in `offending.fields`). Nothing is guessed.
unknown_field.remedy: GET /api/v2/records/describe/<Model>/ lists the fields; rename or drop the ones named and resend the row.

unsupported_intent.meaning: The intent is not one the records endpoint serves.
unsupported_intent.remedy: Use one of: "create" (new records only; an existing record is never overwritten), "upsert" (create, or overwrite exactly the fields you send), "update" (change existing records only), "retract" (move records to the Trash; needs "confirm": "retract"), "restore" (bring a removed batch back), "make_default_set" (make a set the project default; a dry run returns the "confirm" value it needs), or "undo" with a "write_id". There is no hard delete.

unsupported_model.meaning: The records endpoint does not accept this model.
unsupported_model.remedy: Use one of the models listed in `offending.accepted_models`; GET /api/v2/records/describe/<Model>/ describes each.

use_records_endpoint.meaning: A grant tried to write through a resource path. Records are written through ONE endpoint, POST /api/v2/records/.
use_records_endpoint.remedy: POST /api/v2/records/ with {"model": "<Model>", "intent": "create" or "upsert", "records": [...]} — the exact call is in this refusal's `use` key. Validate first with "dry_run": true.

write_access_insufficient.meaning: This credential may read but not write records (its write access is below "records").
write_access_insufficient.remedy: Ask the project owner for a key with records write access (or reconnect the app and allow writing). Reads keep working.

writes_staff_only.meaning: Writing through the API is open to the AI connections of geoDB staff and of members of companies in the geoDB protocol beta for now. Every other key (an organisation or vendor key, anyone else's connection) reads but does not write, whatever write access it was given.
writes_staff_only.remedy: Read with this key, or make the change in the geoDB web app. To join the beta, contact geoDB: https://geodb.io/contact-us/.

above_upper_limit_as_value.meaning: (per-row warning, assays) A value was sent as a plain number above its method's upper limit — more than the method can measure (rulings R-5 / R-v4-1; judged only where the method has an upper limit). It is stored as sent.
above_upper_limit_as_value.remedy: Check with the user: an over-range result is sent as ">" + the upper limit (e.g. ">10000") and the re-assay by an ore-grade method is its value; a units mix-up (ppb sent as ppm) is corrected before writing.

assays_left_unlinked.meaning: (batch warning, retract) Removing these samples (or the hole they belong to) leaves assay records with no live sample of their name. Assays are never removed with their sample: they are kept and re-link if the sample is restored or re-imported. `assays_left_unlinked` in the answer counts them; reads mark them `sample_status: trashed`.
assays_left_unlinked.remedy: Tell the user how many assays will be left without a sample before sending the retract; to keep them linked, restore the sample later (intent "restore") or re-import it under the same name.

below_detection_limit_as_value.meaning: (per-row warning, assays) A value was sent as a plain number below its method's detection limit (ruling R-v4-1). It is stored as sent, as a measured value — not as below detection.
below_detection_limit_as_value.remedy: Check with the user: if the lab reported it below detection, correct the row to "<" + the detection limit (e.g. "<0.2"); if the method's detection limit is wrong, the method needs correcting.

below_detection_stored_otherwise.meaning: (per-row warning) Some values this write touches are stored as a negative number other than -1: below detection, stored before every writer used the -1 sentinel. They are left alone (never converted).
below_detection_stored_otherwise.remedy: Tell the user. If they want them stored as below detection, update each value to "<x" or "BDL" (model "Assay", intent "update", dry run first); otherwise nothing is needed.

beyond_total_depth.meaning: (per-row warning) The interval runs past its hole's recorded total depth; the detail names the hole, its total depth and the depth.
beyond_total_depth.remedy: Check the depth (and its unit) with the user; if the hole was drilled deeper than recorded, the hole's total depth needs correcting instead.

crs_implausible.meaning: (per-row warning) The coordinates look like degrees but the epsg is a projected system, and the writer acknowledged it ("acknowledge": ["crs_implausible"]). Stored exactly as sent; reads mark the row with the same code in `data_warnings`.
crs_implausible.remedy: Check the epsg with the user; if it was wrong, resend the row with the right one (intent "upsert").

date_in_future.meaning: (per-row warning) A date is more than a year in the future (ruling R-v4-2). Stored as sent.
date_in_future.remedy: Check the date with the user (a typo in the year, or a planned date in a field meant for an actual one) and correct it with an update.

depth_units_implausible.meaning: (batch warning) Depths run past the hole's total depth — the mislabeled-units signature (feet under a metres header). The rows landed.
depth_units_implausible.remedy: Check the depth units with the user; if they were wrong, correct the rows (intent "upsert").

detection_limit_not_kept.meaning: (per-row warning) A below-detection result ("<x", or a negative number) is stored as below detection, but its x is not the method's detection limit (or the method has none), so the reported limit is kept nowhere.
detection_limit_not_kept.remedy: Tell the user. If x is the lab's detection limit for this method, write it on the method (model "Method", intent "upsert") before the results — a method is shared by the whole company, so a key that does not reach every project of it is refused out_of_scope, and then the user sets it on the web; otherwise say the reported limit is not stored.

external_id_conflict.meaning: (per-row warning) The row landed, but its external_id already names a different record for this key, so the binding was left unchanged.

external_id_not_recorded.meaning: (per-row warning) The row landed, but its external_id could not be recorded.
external_id_not_recorded.remedy: Re-send the same row with the same external_id; it is a no-op that records the identity.

external_id_shared.meaning: (per-row warning) Another key also uses this external_id in this project. Identities are per key, so this is a separate record.
external_id_shared.remedy: Nothing to do unless the two keys meant the same record; if so, write it through one key only.

file_notice.meaning: (batch warning) A note about the created records (for example a column the model fills on its own).
file_notice.remedy: Read the detail; tell the user if it matters to them.

fuzzy_sample_match.meaning: (per-row warning) A name the row refers to (a laboratory) matched an existing record by resemblance, not exactly; the row is attached to that record. The detail names both.
fuzzy_sample_match.remedy: Confirm with the user that it is the same record; resend with the exact existing name to avoid the warning, or use a clearly different name if it is a different one.

geometry_ring_closed.meaning: (batch warning) A polygon's ring was not closed and was closed for it; the misclosure is reported.
geometry_ring_closed.remedy: If the misclosure is large, check the geometry with the user.

method_detection_limit_missing.meaning: (batch warning) These (method, element) pairs have no detection limit on their method, so a below-detection result keeps no limit at all.
method_detection_limit_missing.remedy: If the lab reported detection limits, write them on the method first (model "Method", intent "upsert", with detection_limit and units), then the results. A method is shared by the whole company: a key that does not reach every project of it is refused out_of_scope, and then the user sets the limit on the web. Tell the user which pairs have none.

point_far_from_project.meaning: (per-row warning) The point is more than 100 km from the rest of the project's located data (ruling R-v4-2) — usually a wrong epsg, swapped coordinates or a missing digit. Stored as sent.
point_far_from_project.remedy: Check the coordinates and their epsg with the user; correct the row with an update (send longitude, latitude and epsg together).

qc_type_missing.meaning: (per-row warning) The sample name looks like a lab QC marker (a standard, blank or duplicate) but the row carries no qc_type, so it lands as a routine sample and never reaches the QAQC checks.
qc_type_missing.remedy: Ask the user whether it is QC. If it is, resend the row with its qc_type (and the standard it is); if it is a real sample id, go on.

sample_link_changes.meaning: (per-row warning, assay rename) An assay is linked to its sample by name, so renaming it moves its results: `from` is the sample of the old name, `to` the sample of the new one (null: no sample has that name and the assay is unlinked).
sample_link_changes.remedy: Tell the user which sample the results move to, or that they will be unlinked, before sending the rename; Undo puts the old name back.

sample_not_linked.meaning: (per-row warning) No sample of this name exists in the project, so the result is stored but waits unlinked to any sample. A misspelt sample name is the usual cause.
sample_not_linked.remedy: Compare the name with the project's samples (read drill-samples/ or point-samples/); if it is misspelt, correct it before the write. If the sample is simply not written yet, say so to the user: it links when it is.

set_exists_derived_from_ignored.meaning: (per-row warning) The request asked to create a set that already exists, so the rows went into that existing set and the "derived_from" sent with it was NOT recorded (an existing set's provenance is never rewritten).
set_exists_derived_from_ignored.remedy: If this is a new derived interpretation, send it into a NEW set name with "create": true and its "derived_from"; otherwise leave "derived_from" out.

stored_differently.meaning: (per-row warning) The row WAS written, but the stored values differ from what was sent (geoDB normalised them); `conflicts` lists each field with `stored` and `sent`. The row is not refused and Undo reaches it.
stored_differently.remedy: Read the record back and tell the user how it was stored; if the sent value must win, correct it with an update.

stored_values_changed.meaning: (per-row warning) The configuration change also rewrote values stored on records (a custom column's type conversion, or a choice renamed or replaced); `detail` says how many. Undo reverses them.
stored_values_changed.remedy: Tell the user how many records changed; if that was not wanted, undo the write with its write_id.

survey_dogleg.meaning: (per-row warning) The survey station bends the hole more than 20° per 30 m from its nearest station (ruling R-v4-2) — usually a typo, or magnetic and grid azimuths mixed. Stored as sent.
survey_dogleg.remedy: Check the azimuth and dip with the user; correct the station with an update.

value_rounded.meaning: (per-row warning) The value has more decimal places than the database keeps; it is stored rounded. The detail names the value sent and the value stored.
value_rounded.remedy: Nothing is refused. Tell the user the value is stored rounded; if the extra precision matters, it is lost here.

value_unit_impossible.meaning: (per-row warning) The value is physically impossible in its unit (more than 100 %, 1,000,000 ppm or 1,000,000,000 ppb). A unit mix-up (ppb read as ppm, a fraction read as percent) or a typo is the usual cause. It is stored as sent.
value_unit_impossible.remedy: Show the user the value and its unit before the write; correct the value or the unit, and never change it without asking.

value_unparseable.meaning: (per-row warning) The result is neither a number nor a lab status; nothing is stored for it.
value_unparseable.remedy: Ask the user what the lab meant, correct the value (a number, "<x", ">x" or a lab status) and resend the row.

values_skipped_record_exists.meaning: (write-level warning) A create SKIPPED value rows because their record (a sample, a method, a standard) already exists: nothing was stored for them — a create never adds values to an existing record. `records` and `rows` name them; `created_by_this_key` lists the records an EARLIER write of this key created (a record's rows were split across requests). `summary.skipped_by_reason` counts them.
values_skipped_record_exists.remedy: Tell the user. To store those values, resend exactly the rows named in `rows` with "intent": "upsert" (dry run first; Undo removes exactly the values it adds); a row that would CHANGE a stored value also needs "acknowledge": ["replace_values"] after the user agrees. Next time keep every row of one record in ONE request.

write_not_recorded.meaning: (batch warning) The rows landed but the write record failed; the audit batch id is in the detail.
write_not_recorded.remedy: Keep the audit batch id from the detail and tell the user; report it through POST /api/v2/feedback/.
